newsitem.title: GERMANY: Statement on revaluing German currency reserves.
newsitem.headline: Statement on revaluing German currency reserves.

text.p: The following is the text of a joint statement issued by German Finance Minister Theo Waigel and Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer on Thursday on plans to revalue central bank currency reserves.

"The transition to the third state of currency union demands changes in the balance sheet structure of the Bundesbank and its accounting rules. Without prejudicing the federal legislature, an agreement exists between the German government and the Bundesbank on the measures leading to this.

1. The capital structure of the Bundesbank will be placed on a new legal basis with the transition to the third stage of monetary union. The (Bundesbank's) capital will be increased substantially and the legal reserves will be established on an equally high level.

2. Along with the transition to the third stage of monetary union, existing rules governing the Bundesbank's accounting will be remodelled. This will make it possible for the Bundesbank to adapt its accounting to the basic methods which will apply to the European Central Bank. The Bundesbank intends to make use of this possibility.

According to the basic ruling by the European Monetary Institute, the adjustment makes an assessment near to the market value of currency reserves and the placing of the formerly-hidden reserves into a new valuation reserve, which will serve to balance out currency risks and fluctuations in valuation.

3. In view of the planned transition to the third stage of monetary union, the Bundesbank intends to use available manoeuvring room for evaluation for the 1997 business year which is contained in the current accounting rules. These allow an evaluation of the currency reserves closer to the market while maintaining the principle of lowest value.
Suggestions for the necessary legal measures will be developed with the Bundesbank and presented to the legislature as an addition to the draft law amending the Bundesbank law.
